verdicts.reason: Directly stated in INT-VER-001; scenario check is appropriate.

INT-VER-002 states that near-2^64 behaviour shall be reached by writing the timer value registers. The 'WHEN' text is only a rationale, but the rule itself is correct and can be exercised in a scenario.

questions.question: INT-VER-001 says 'through the ports above', but the ports are not part of the quote. Which ports (bus interface, interrupt, alert) are allowed for observing each item?
What is the expected response for each bus error case (unmapped address, sub-word write, instruction fetch, integrity error), and when does fatal_fault assert? The quote does not say.
Which registers does 'timer value registers' cover (lower and upper halves)? Is a write to one half atomic with respect to counting?
